briefdescription.para: Appends the shortest decimal representation of a numeric value to a buffer.

detaileddescription.para:
T
The numeric type to format.
buffer
The string to append to.
v
The value to format.
Returns
Nothing.
The value is formatted into a local buffer, which is then appended to buffer.

For long double, a platform-specific path is chosen:
On Windows and on platforms where long double has the same storage width as double (e.g. 32-bit Arm), the value is cast to double and formatted with std::to_chars.
On all other platforms (e.g. x86-64 Linux/macOS with 80-bit extended precision, or AArch64 and RISC-V with 128-bit quad precision), snprintf with %.*Lg is used as a portable fallback, because std::to_chars for long double may be unavailable (e.g. when linking with lld). The precision starts at LDBL_DIG and is increased until the text reads back, with strtold, as the same value, up to LDBL_DECIMAL_DIG, which always reads back exactly. This gives the shortest exact form, as std::to_chars gives for the other types; a shorter form would need fewer than LDBL_DIG digits, and Lg removes the trailing zeros, so starting at LDBL_DIG does not lose it. For zero and the subnormal values, which have fewer significant digits, the precision starts at 1. The value of errno, which strtold may set for subnormal values, is preserved. If no precision reads back exactly, the C library handles long double with the precision of double (e.g. newlib on AArch64 and RISC-V), and the value is cast to double and formatted with std::to_chars, as above.

For all other numeric types, std::to_chars is called directly, providing locale-independent formatting. The snprintf() path uses the decimal point of the C locale, which is . unless the application changes it with setlocale().

briefdescription.para: Appends the hexadecimal address of a pointer to a buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Shared by the reporter and the expression_formatter, so that the pointers are displayed identically in the messages and in the expressions. Pointers to const or volatile objects, and function pointers, are accepted too.

T
The type pointed to (an object or a function type).
buffer
The string to append to.
v
The pointer.
Returns
Nothing.
Null pointers are rendered as "0x0", regardless of the platform, avoiding platform-specific representations such as "(nil)" on Linux/glibc. Non-null pointers are formatted with snprintf(), using the p specifier.

The p specifier expects a void*. Object pointers are converted implicitly to const volatile void*, which accepts any qualification, and the qualifiers are then removed with const_cast; a reinterpret_cast to void* would not compile for pointers to const objects. The object is not accessed. Function pointers, which do not convert to void* implicitly, use reinterpret_cast.

briefdescription.para: Converts an integer or a character to the type used to compare it.

detaileddescription.para: The conversion keeps the value, since the type has the same size and signedness. Applied to both operands of the std::cmp_*() functions, which do not accept the character types.

briefdescription.para: Prepares an operand of a comparator.

detaileddescription.para: The arrays and the pointers of the character types (char, wchar_t, char8_t, char16_t, and char32_t, but not signed char or unsigned char, which are byte buffers) are converted to basic_c_string, so that they are compared by content; the other arrays, including those of volatile characters, are converted to array_operand, so that they are compared element by element, the functions to function pointers, and all other operands are returned unchanged, so the other pointers, including the pointers to volatile characters, and the functions are compared by address.
The other operands are forwarded, so that the comparator moves a temporary, and refers to a named operand.

T
The type deduced for the forwarding reference.
t
The operand.
A basic_c_string for the C strings, an array_operand for the other arrays, otherwise t, forwarded.
Arrays of the character types are converted using their size as a bound, pointers to them using the null terminator; the const qualifier of the characters is ignored. The volatile characters are not strings, since basic_c_string cannot refer to them: an array of them is converted to array_operand, like the other arrays, and compared element by element, and a pointer to them is forwarded, and compared by address, like the other pointers. The functions are converted to function pointers. Every other operand is forwarded, unchanged, as an lvalue or an rvalue reference.

The qualifiers of an array are those of its elements, so the element type is taken from the type of the argument, not from the type without qualifiers, which would lose the volatile of the elements, and the conversion to the pointer to const elements would not compile.

briefdescription.para: Tells whether two numbers differ by at most a tolerance.

detaileddescription.para: If the three values are integers, the distance is computed exactly, as an unsigned value, also for operands of mixed signedness, and compared with the tolerance with std::cmp_less_equal(), so that neither overflows nor wraps around. Otherwise, the values are converted to their common floating-point type, and the absolute value of the difference is compared with the tolerance. A negative tolerance, or a NaN, makes the result false.

Lhs_T
The arithmetic type of the first value.
Rhs_T
The arithmetic type of the second value.
Epsilon_T
The arithmetic type of the tolerance.
lhs
The first value.
rhs
The second value.
epsilon
The tolerance.
true
The distance between the values is less than or equal to the tolerance.
false
Otherwise.
For the integers, the larger value is selected with std::cmp_less(), and the distance is computed in std::uintmax_t: when both values have the same sign, as the modular difference of their conversions, which is exact; otherwise, as the sum of the larger value and of the magnitude of the negative one. A sum that does not fit in std::uintmax_t is flagged as an overflow, and gives false, since the true distance is larger than any tolerance. The tolerance is compared with std::cmp_less_equal(), so a negative one gives false.

For the other types, the values are converted to their common type, which is a floating-point one, so std::int64_t values compared with a float tolerance lose precision; the comparison is inclusive, so a distance equal to the tolerance succeeds. Two equal values, including two infinities of the same sign, whose difference would be NaN, are at the distance zero; a NaN operand always fails.

briefdescription.para: Stops the compilation of a compare_op whose tag is rejected, with a message that tells why.

detaileddescription.para: Always fails the static assertion that applies, since it is called only when extension::compare_tag is not satisfied: the missing or unprintable symbol is reported first, then the apply() that cannot be called with the operands, or whose result is not convertible to bool.

briefdescription.para: Stops the compilation of a comparator whose operands are rejected, with a message that tells why.

detaileddescription.para: Always fails the static assertion that applies, since it is called only when comparable_operands is not satisfied: an operand that cannot be written is reported first, then the operator that the operands do not support. Called by the overloads of the comparators that accept the rejected operands, so that the compiler shows this message instead of a list of the unsatisfied constraints.

parameterdescription.para: The type of the left operand.
The type of the right operand.

briefdescription.para: Stops the compilation of a predicate_op whose tag is rejected, with a message that tells why.

detaileddescription.para: As reject_compare_tag(), for the tag of a predicate, whose apply() takes one operand; called only when extension::predicate_tag is not satisfied.

briefdescription.para: Returns the value wrapped by a framework type, or the operand itself.

detaileddescription.para: If the type T is a framework expression type (see extension::is_op) that provides a get() member function, it is invoked and its result returned. Otherwise a reference to the argument itself is returned, so that the types of the application, even those with a get() member function, are compared with their own operators, without a copy. The selection is performed at compile time via if constexpr with an inline requires expression; the return type is deduced with decltype (auto) from the selected branch.
Always call it qualified, as detail::unwrap(), so that argument-dependent lookup cannot select a function of the application, defined in the namespace of an operand.
The operand is returned by reference, without a copy; the result is valid only as long as the operand.

simplesect.para: The value returned by t.get() for the framework wrappers (the literals and the to_* wrappers), otherwise a reference to t.

briefdescription.para: C++ header file with inline implementations for the µTest++ internal detail namespace.

detaileddescription.para: This header provides the out-of-line template and inline implementations for all types declared in detail.h. It defines the bodies of the unwrap() helper, the unary and binary operator base class templates, the comparison tags, all relational, approximate, and logical comparator constructors, the predicate constructor, the tolerance helpers (within_tolerance(), differ_by_at_most()), the callable operator types (throws_op, nothrow_op), the append_number() and append_pointer() formatting helpers, the basic_c_string operand and its operators, and as_operand().
Separating the implementations from the declarations keeps detail.h concise and focused on the interface, whilst grouping the complex lambda-based constructor bodies here for maintainability.
All definitions reside within the micro_os_plus::micro_test_plus::detail namespace.
This file is included by detail.h; the applications include micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus.h, not this file.
